Tanvir, you said your friend Rohit has stopped coming to class? Let your Sudha Masi tell you about my friend Leena, back in college in Nagpur. She was the loudest girl in our hostel, always organising picnics. Then she failed economics in second year. Suddenly she was skipping lectures, sleeping till noon, changing the subject whenever anyone said "exam". The others lectured her: "You'll ruin your future!" She hid even more.
I didn't lecture. One morning I knocked with two cups of chai and said, "Come with me to the library for one hour. We'll just find out the re-exam date. That's all." She came. The next week we did one chapter together. She passed in December. So, beta, don't give your friend a speech. Give him company and one small step.

qa.a: Economics, in second year.

qa.q: Why might Leena have hidden even more when the others lectured her?
qa.a: She probably felt ashamed about failing, and lectures made the shame bigger, so avoiding people and exams felt safer.

qa.q: What choice of Sudha's helped Leena, and why?
qa.a: Bringing chai and asking for just one hour to find the re-exam date, which offered company and a small step instead of pressure.

qa.q: How might Tanvir use this story with Rohit?
qa.a: Tanvir could skip the speech and offer Rohit company and one small, concrete step, like checking a date together.

Himani, who usually sang in the corridor and dragged everyone to the chai stall, now slept through lectures and turned her face to the wall whenever anyone mentioned statistics, the paper she had failed.

"Let's just download last year's paper. Ten minutes. Then biscuits." Himani hesitated, then sat up. The Wi-Fi kept dropping in the rain, so they used Sarita's phone data. They opened the paper, read question one, and ate the biscuits.
On Wednesday, Himani knocked on Sarita's door.

"Maria! You weren't in lab again."

Maria looked at the ground. "Three?"

"Three. I'll wait by the stairs."

At five to three, Maria was at the stairs, her hood up, but there.

I'm Gopika, and this was in our second year of engineering in Thrissur. Arnab was the loudest person in quiz club. He ran it, basically. Then he failed Engineering Drawing, and he vanished.

At first I didn't connect it. He just missed quiz one week. Then he stopped coming to the drawing studio. In the canteen, if anyone said "backlog", he suddenly needed to take a call.

I wanted to shake him and say, "You'll lose a year!" But I remembered how I felt when my uncle lectured me after my twelfth results. I just curled up.

So one Friday I texted him: "I'm redoing my sheet 3 in the studio tomorrow at ten. Bring your pencils. We'll do one sheet. Just one."

He replied an hour later: "ok."

He came late. He did half the sheet. But he came back the Saturday after.

qa.q: What did Arnab suddenly need to do when someone in the canteen said "backlog"?
qa.a: He suddenly needed to take a call.

qa.q: Why did Gopika decide not to shake Arnab and warn him about losing a year?
qa.a: Gopika remembered feeling small and curling up when an uncle lectured after the twelfth results, and was worried a lecture would push Arnab further away.

qa.q: What was the turning point in how Gopika helped Arnab?
qa.a: Choosing a concrete invitation, one sheet in the studio at ten, instead of a warning. A specific small step with company was easier for Arnab to accept.

qa.q: What might the text "ok", an hour later, tell us about Arnab?
qa.a: It may show he was hesitant or embarrassed but still willing. The delay suggests saying yes wasn't easy for him.

Diary, Imran.

Alka hasn't been to organic chemistry in eleven days. She failed the mid-sem and since then, if anyone mentions it, she laughs and says, "Who cares," and walks off. She used to be the loudest person in our lab group. Now she eats in her room.

I almost gave her a speech today. "You'll fail the whole year," etc. I stopped. That's what her parents are probably already saying.

Instead, at the hostel gate, I said, "I'm going to the library at five. I'll sit at the corner table. You could come, or not. If you do, we could just do one page of the reaction notes together. One page."

She didn't answer. At five-fifteen she walked in and sat down. We did one page. She didn't say much. But she stayed.

In Madrid, Kaito was the one who always knew the cheapest tapas and the best free concerts. Then he failed Statistics II, and Diego watched him fold inward.

He missed three seminars in a row. He stopped replying in the course group chat. When Diego mentioned the resit, Kaito said, "Let's not talk about uni," and put on music. One night Diego saw his light still on at four in the morning, the resit syllabus open and untouched beside a video game.

Diego didn't say, "You need to get serious." He had seen how that made people hide more. Instead, the next morning, he knocked with two coffees. "I have a free hour. Want to do just the first practice question together? Then churros."

Kaito hesitated at the door. Then he stepped back and let Diego in.

qa.a: Kaito failed Statistics II.

qa.a: Diego felt worried for Kaito and knew lectures make people hide more, so he chose a gentler approach.
